answer: Give every agent an acoustic fingerprint. At random times the network asks for ten seconds of room sound, fan hum, street traffic, a kettle boiling, hashed on the spot. A real room is an oasis of messy, unrepeatable noise in an ocean of clean synthetic audio; no two rooms share the same hum. Clones replaying one recording get caught when their clips match. Forging an identity means staging a distinct acoustic space, a rented room or a sable foam booth with its own speakers, about $40 a month each plus hardware. Like a voiceprint for a place, it proves the agent lives somewhere real.
